creator: anna.zhang
caption:
creative coding to rethink what a camera can be… beyond a device that records a scene literally but one that changes the way you notice what’s happening around you 📹

Change Capture filters out anything that stays the same between frames. What’s left is not a traditional photograph, but a trace of movement and time. A butterfly leaving the frame, rain hitting the pavement, branches swaying in the wind… small moments that usually disappear into the background become the subject.

I wanted to make a camera that resists the quick snapshot. One that asks you to slow down, stay with what’s in front of you, and notice the tiny changes unfolding in your environment.

Try it out: 🔗 change-capture.anna-zhang.com (link also in bio!)

Original videos:
Dandelions gently sway in a peaceful field during a warm sunset by NSU MON
A serene view of birds flying freely in a clear blue sky, capturing nature’s beauty by Manas Ranjan Sahoo
A blue airplane flies high with vapor trails against a bright sky by Dave Planes
Close-up of a butterfly on vibrant flowers in a peaceful garden setting by Tường Chopper
Calm water ripples creating mesmerizing patterns in slow motion by Hobi Photography
Seagulls Soaring in Azure Sky Footage by Diana ✨

#creativecoding #codeart #videoart #creativetechnology #videoeffects
transcript: I made Change Capture, a camera that only captures what changes. It ignores everything still, so the image becomes less about what a place looks like and more about what happened there. A butterfly flying away, raindrops falling onto the ground, a tree swaying in the wind. The tiny things you only notice when you stay with the scene for a little longer. Interested in cameras not just as tools for documenting, but as tools for changing how we pay attention. Change Capture slows the act of taking a photo down. Instead of instantly grabbing a perfect image, I wanted to create something that would make you wait and watch, and notice what the world is doing in between moments.

creator: stics.ai
caption:
🚨 Claude can be used like an executive function coach.

Instead of forcing yourself to “just focus,” you can use the right prompts to break tasks down, reduce overwhelm, create momentum, and stay on track.
Here are 7 useful prompts to try:

1. The Task Paralysis Breaker
Prompt:
“I’m staring at [Task] and I can’t start. Break it into ridiculously small steps that each take less than 1 minute. Give me the very first step and tell me exactly what to do with my hands to begin.”

2. The Dopamine Menu Builder
Prompt:
“I’m feeling under-stimulated. Create a dopamine menu for me with 5-minute appetizers for quick movement, 20-minute entrees for deep work, and 10-minute sides for creative play so I can stay engaged.”

3. The Virtual Body Double
Prompt:
“Act as my virtual body double for the next 30 minutes. I’ll tell you what I’m working on, and I want you to check in every 10 minutes to ask for a status update and help keep me focused.”

4. The Context-Switching Reset
Prompt:
“I just finished [Task A] and need to start [Task B], but my brain is stuck. Create a 3-minute mental reset routine to help me switch between these two tasks.”

5. The Boring Task Gamifier
Prompt:
“I have a boring task: [Task]. Help me gamify it by connecting it to my current interest: [Interest]. Turn it into a quest where completing the task unlocks a reward.”

6. The Time-Blindness Reality Check
Prompt:
“I think [Project] will take 20 minutes, but it usually takes much longer. Help me time-map it by identifying 3 hidden sub-tasks I might be forgetting so I can set a realistic deadline.”

7. The Open Loops Organizer
Prompt:
“My brain feels full of open loops. I’ll dump everything I’m worried about below. Categorize them into Now, Later, and Trash, then give me a one-sentence next step for each Now item.”

caption:
The hottest new job in AI is the Forward Deployed Engineer. This is what they actually do — could this be you?

#ainews #aitools #forwarddeployedengineer #engineering #buildinpublic
transcript: The hardest job in AI that nobody is talking about is no longer the prompt engineer or even the AI engineer. It's called the Forward Deployed Engineer, and balance your basically invented it over a decade ago. But now the corporate push for AI is making it explode and companies like OpenAI and Thropic are just hiring for it like crazy. So here's what they actually do. Instead of sitting behind a computer and building a feature or building a product, FDE is basically working the field. They are embedded directly in a client's company, and they become the bridge between the AI product and how the company actually runs day-to-day. They identify opportunities and blockers in things like a company's workflow, legacy infrastructure, messy data, and create seamless integrations, automated pipelines, secure and compliance setups. That's still part of this whole AI boom that nobody's really talking about, and a price AI doesn't fail because the model is bad. It fails because connecting it to a 15-year-old database with weird security constraints, a ton of undocumented stuff requires one specialized human, and that is the FDE. So, if you're full stack, you like working with people, problem-solving, and want to be in the AI space, this might be for you.
